doc.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: First record date with John Lewis, Percy Heath and Connie Kay
summary: Meeting John Lewis at a Modern Jazz Quartet concert led to his first American record, Jazz Piano International.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Who did you start working with?

Oh, well. All right. That’s another story. This is, I’ve been in the country two weeks, no a week, and my wife and I, we’d run out of money because we’d stayed in a hotel in New York and we said well we can’t live here, it’s too much money. So we found an apartment in Brooklyn. And I looked in the local paper, and I saw there was a concert by the Modern Jazz Quartet at Brooklyn Academy of Music. So I said, I’ve got to try, I love those guys. You know I’d managed to hear it at some time. And so I got there very early. And there was John Lewis, you know, the leader, and he’s putting programs on every seat. You know John took care of everything. He wrote the music, he made the guys rehearse, and he put the programs — he did everything. And I don’t know why, I’m

usually a kind of reserved guy, but I started getting into a conversation. And he said, “oh I know you.” I said, “how could you possibly know me?” He said, “well I subscribe to this English periodical it’s called ‘The Gramophone’ and they review jazz records. And you made a record in England and I have it.” I said, “what!” And I couldn’t believe it. He said, “by the way, what are you doing tomorrow night?” And believe me, I don’t make up these stories, it’s stranger than fiction. I said, “what do you mean, I’m doing nothing.” He said, “please be at Atlantic Recording Studios and we’ll record something.” So I’d been there two weeks and I made my first record. And it was with Percy Heath and Connie Kay — not a bad rhythm section. But of course I was so damn nervous that, you know. I’ve got the record at home it’s not really very good.
Well what was the role with the, I mean, you were both piano players so what was he having—

He was making, it came out, the album was called “Jazz Piano International.” So he got me and I was representing England, and he got a French pianist by the name of René Urtreger, and we all played like four tracks. And Dick Katz was there who was the American piano player. And that’s how the album came out.
